identity.title: ALMA Observations of Molecular Absorption in the Gravitational Lens PMN 0134-0931 at z = 0.7645

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report the detection of molecular absorption lines at $z$=0.7645 towards the radio-loud QSO PMN 0134-0931.

evidence.quote: The lens itself has not been reliably detected as it is overpowered by the glare of the background, $z_s$=2.2 QSO
The lens itself has not been reliably detected as it is overpowered by the glare of the background, $z_s$=2.2 QSO

distance_source.value: Absorption redshift; z_s from Gregg et al. 2002; Winn & Keeton 2003

evidence.quote: The lens itself has not been reliably detected as it is overpowered by the glare of the background, $z_s$=2.2 QSO

question.value: Do the lensing galaxies of PMN 0134-0931 at z=0.7645 show CO and HCO+ J=2-1 absorption along different lensed lines of sight, and what do the kinematics and column densities reveal about the molecular gas?

evidence.quote: The CO J=2–1 and HCO$^+$ J=2–1 lines are seen in absorption along two different lines of sight to lensed images of the background QSO.
under ALMA Cycle 3 project 2015.1.00582.S
redshifted into ALMA bands 3 and 4, respectively (hereafter B3 and B4)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two 1.875 GHz basebands per band, 1920 channels, 976.563 kHz; plus two 2 GHz continuum basebands with 128 channels; high-res centered at 101.007 and 130.276 GHz

evidence.quote: For each band we used two basebands of width 1.875 GHz and 1920 channels giving a spectral resolution of 976.563 kHz.
We observed the CO J=2–1 and HCO$^+$ J=2–1 transitions
We observed the CO J=2–1 and HCO$^+$ J=2–1 transitions

continuum_bandwidth.value: ~4 GHz combined, centered 91 GHz (B3) and 140 GHz (B4)

evidence.quote: each with a combined bandwidth of $\sim$4 GHz
The longest baseline was 2.48 km, with a nominal angular resolution of 0$\,.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$28.

angular_resolution.value: nominal 0.35" (B3), 0.28" (B4); best continuum 0.24"x0.18" at 140 GHz uniform

evidence.quote: The highest angular resolution (0$\,.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$24$\times$0$\,.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$18) is obtained at 140 GHz using uniform weighting
The total on-source time for the B4 observation was $\sim$67 minutes.
September 9 (B4), September 17 and 19 (B3), 2016 under ALMA Cycle 3 project 2015.1.00582.S

what.value: Radio continuum component positions and flux densities (15 GHz, spectral index -0.69) used for lens comparison and covering factors

evidence.quote: The location and relative flux levels are taken from Winn & Keeton (2003).

what.value: OH 1667 MHz 4-component Gaussian fit and HI 21cm profile

evidence.quote: Kanekar et al. (2012) provide a 4-component Gaussian fit to their OH 1667 MHz spectrum

what.value: Lens model with two galaxies of similar mass

evidence.quote: The two lensing galaxies, called Gal-N and Gal-S in Keeton & Winn (2003), are of similar mass
The data reduction and calibration was done with the CASA[^3] package following standard procedures.

flux_calibrator.value: J0006-0623 (also bandpass), bootstrapped to Solar system objects

evidence.quote: The bright quasar J0006-0623 was used as both bandpass and flux calibrator.
The overall flux accuracy is better than $\sim$10% in both B3 and B4.

weighting_robust.value: Briggs, robust = 0.5 for spectral cubes; uniform for highest-resolution continuum

evidence.quote: The data cubes used for extracting the spectra were cleaned using Briggs weighting with the robustness set to 0.5.

what.value: Lens component designation and positions follow Winn & Keeton (2003)

evidence.quote: We use the same designation of the lens components as in Winn & Keeton (2003).

method.value: Continuum images from continuum basebands; component fluxes and positions tabulated

evidence.quote: The continuum data was used to construct images of the PMN 0134-0931 system.

validation.value: Compared positions and flux ratios with radio images of Winn & Keeton (2003)

evidence.quote: Overall, the flux ratios seen at radio frequencies are consistent with our results at millimeter wavelengths

analysis_steps.goal: Extract absorption spectra and fit Gaussians

method.value: Spectra extracted with aperture equal to restoring beam toward A-C and D from Briggs cubes; Gaussian fits

evidence.quote: We used an aperture with the same size as the restoring beam to extract spectra towards the continuum images A-C and D in PMN 0134-0931.

key_parameters.value: Briggs robust 0.5; 3 Gaussians for D, 2 for A-C

evidence.quote: The A-C component only requires two Gaussian components to give a good fit.

fitting.value: Non-linear Gaussian fit; errors from covariance matrix

evidence.quote: The error estimates of the Gaussian components are derived from the covariance matrix of the non-linear fit.

validation.value: Velocity difference estimated three ways, consistent

evidence.quote: All of these estimates are consistent with each other within the errors

method.value: tau = -ln(1-F); LTE column density from integrated opacity

evidence.quote:
The observed opacity can be directly derived from the normalized flux $F(
u)$ shown in Fig. [3](#fig:molabs) as $	au_{
u_{obs}} = -\ln{(1 - F(
u))}$.
Assuming that $f_{c} = 1$ and consequently, $\tau_{\nu} = \tau_{\nu_{obs}}$

method.value: 1.0" aperture spectrum binned to 13.4 km/s; 5 sigma limit on H2 mass

evidence.quote: No emission was detected and assuming a velocity width of 200 km s$^{-1}$ the 5$\sigma$ upper limit to the molecular mass is $3.5 \times 10^{9}$ M$_{\odot}$.
We used $\alpha = 4.6$ M$_{\odot}$ (km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$)$^{-1}$ for the conversion between CO luminosity and H$_2$ mass.
The data reduction and calibration was done with the CASA[^3] package following standard procedures.

results_numeric.quantity: Velocity difference between A-C and D absorption

evidence.quote: we adopt $\Delta$v = 215$\pm8$ km s$^{-1}$
The ratio of $N_{CO}/N_{HCO^+}$ is $\sim$500 towards the A-C component and $\sim$1500 towards the D component.
The average spectral index is $\alpha = -1.6$

results_numeric.quantity: 5 sigma upper limit on molecular mass

evidence.quote: the 5$\sigma$ upper limit to the molecular mass is $3.5 \times 10^{9}$ M$_{\odot}$

findings_qualitative.value: CO and HCO+ absorption toward D is unusually strong, suggesting dense molecular gas; widths suggest inclined disk with flat rotation curve

evidence.quote: It is plausible that the second line of sight probes denser molecular gas than what is normally the case for absorption.

claims.hypothesis: Do both lensed sightlines show molecular absorption with a velocity offset?
claims.experiment: Extract CO and HCO+ spectra toward A-C and D and fit Gaussians
claims.finding: Possible rotation of a lensing galaxy, though interaction may disturb kinematics

evidence.quote: The absorption lines through the two lines of sight are shifted by 215 $\pm$ 8 km s$^{-1}$, possibly representing rotational motion in one of the lensing galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Is the gas along D typical diffuse gas?

evidence.quote: Also, the abundance ratio $N_{CO}/N_{HCO^+}$ is $2-3$ times higher than in typical diffuse molecular gas.

why_this_method.value: Briggs robust 0.5 maximizes sensitivity while still separating continuum components

evidence.quote: but is necessary to maximize the sensitivity while still retaining sufficient angular resolution to separate the continuum components

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Uniform weighting for spectra rejected as too noisy

evidence.quote: A uniform weighting produced noisy spectral data

limitations_admitted.value: Lens galaxy location and orientation unknown, limiting interpretation

evidence.quote: The interpretation is currently hampered by the lack of accurate information on the location and orientation of the lensing galaxies.

referee_caveats_inferred: Covering factor assumed unity; N_CO/N_HCO+ may reflect f_c<1
Excitation temperature for column densities not stated
Continuum level taken from line basebands; method unclear

missing_for_reproduction: Tx and rest frequencies for column densities
reproducibility.score_reason: Public ALMA project and clear recipe, but many processing and imaging details unstated.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple spectra, numeric results in tables.

companion_papers.why: Earlier HI, OH and HCO+ observations of the same lens
